Diastereoselective Construction of Cyclopent-2-enone-4-ols from 
Aldehydes and 1,2-Allenones Catalyzed by N-Heterocyclic Carbene  
Dengke Ma, Chunling Fu and Shengming Ma* 
Cyclopent-2-enone-4-ols have been prepared highly 
diastereoselectively from readily available aromati c aldehydes 
and 1,2-allenones catalyzed by N-heterocyclic carbene. 
Mechanistic studies showed that there are four possible pathways. 
Cyclopent-2-enone-4-ol unit exists in some natural products 
and biological active compounds, 1 thus, efficient synthetic 
routes to these compounds are of high interest. 2 Known 
methods for their preparations from acyclic precurs ors 
includes: cyclizations of 1,2-diketones with 3-oxoc arboxylic 
acid esters or amides, 3 ketones, 4 1,3-bis(trimethylsiloxy)-1,3-
dienes,3a,5 2-(trimethylsiloxy)allyltriemthylsilane, 6 or 2,3-
allenoates;7 transition metal-catalyzed intramolecular coupling 
of ethyl 3-(triethylsilyloxy)-5-(tributylstannyl)pe nt-4(Z)-
enthioates followed by desilylation; 8 ring closing metathesis of 
5-OTBS or DPS-hepta-1,6-dien-3-ones followed by pos sible 
deprotection;9 Tandem Aldol–Brook reaction of β-
(phenylthio)acryloyl silanes with lithium enolates followed by 
simultaneous desilylation and dephenylthiolation; 10  tandem 
ozonolysis–Knoevenagel cyclization of tert -butyl 5-OTBS-3-
oxohept-6-enoates;11  Nazarov reaction and desiylation of ( E)-
4-methoxymethyl-1-silyloxyhexa-1,4,5-trien-3-ols;12  and the 
cyclization reactions involving cis -2-en-1,4-diketones 13  or ( Z)-4-
oxopent-2-enal.14 
On the other hand, traditionally,  the treatment of aldehydes 
with N-heterocyclic carbenes would afford the Breslow 
intermediate, subsequent Michael addition with α,β-
unsaturated carbonyl compounds gave 1,4-diketones ( the 
Stetter reaction) (Scheme 1, eq 1). 
15,16 We hypothesized that 
when 1,2-allenone is treated with the Breslow inter mediate, a 
mixture of C-C double bonds regio-isomers 1,4-diket ones S3 , 
S4  and S5 , could be produced. Rather unexpectedly, the cycli c 
4-hydroxycyclopentenone product was formed highly 
diastereoselectively (Scheme 1, eq 2). 
 
Scheme 1 Stetter reaction and this reaction. 
In the beginning, we attempted the reaction of 4-
bromobenzaldehyde 
1a  with 1,2-allenyl ketone 2a  using 
Cs 2CO 3 as the base and toluene as the solvent in the pres ence 
of different commercially available N-hetereocyclic carbene 
precursors A to E. In addition to the C=C bond regio-isomer 
4aa , ( E)-3aa , and ( Z)-3aa , a new cyclic product 5aa  (dr = 95:5) 
was observed in 40% yield when changing the solvent  from 
toluene to dioxane (Table S1, entry 10, see ESI†). 
Inspired by the observation above, reaction paramet ers 
including the loading of the NHC precursor 
A1  and Cs 2CO 3, 
solvents, together with the reaction temperature we re 
screened extensively. As a result, increasing the l oading of 
Cs 2CO 3 led to a complete transformation to product 5aa . 
However, the diastereoselectivity was not satisfact ory (Table 1, 
entry 1). Running the reaction at 10 oC gave a better 
diastereoselectivity with a lower yield (Table 1, e ntry 3). By 
reducing the loading of base, a slightly higher 
diastereoselectivity was observed with a lower yiel d (Table 1, 
entries 4 and 5). As expected, the reaction at 50 
 oC afforded 
the product 5aa  with a lower diastereoselectivity (81:19), 
although the yield is 68% (Table 1, entry 6). After  further 
optimization, the best diastereoselectivity was obt ained with 
10 mol % A1  and 25 mol % Cs 2CO 3 using dioxane as solvent at 
15 oC (Table 1, entry 8). Other solvents, such as DMF, THF and 
CH 3CN didn’t give a better result (Table 1, entries 11-13).

The reaction of aliphatic aldehyde 1f  was also studied. 
Nevertheless, the expected 4-alkyl substituted cycl opent-2-
enone-4-ol was not formed, only 6% of 6fa  was observed, 
together with 58% recovery of aldehyde 1f  and 39% recovery 
of 1,2-allenone 2a  (Scheme 2). Obviously, the reactivity of 
aliphatic aldehyde towards NHC precursor A1  is rather low in 
such a reaction. 
 
Scheme 2 The reaction of aliphatic aldehyde 1f . 
In order to gain insight into the reaction, possibl e intermediate 
(E)-3ba  and ( Z)-3ba  were isolated utilizing the condition of 
entry 1 in Table S1 (see ESI†). As a result, cyclic product 5ba  
couldn’t be formed when starting from ( E)-3ba  under sole 20 
mol % of Cs 2CO 3 (Scheme 3, eq 1) or under 20 mol % of A1  and 
Cs 2CO 3, respectively (Scheme 3, eq 3). On the other hand,  ( Z)-
3ba  also couldn’t be transferred to 5ba  catalyzed only by 20 
mol % of Cs 2CO 3 (Scheme 3, eq 2). However, 5ba  was obtained 
in only 34% NMR yield (dr = 97:3) together with 3% of 4ba  
when 20 mol % of A1  and 20 mol % of Cs 2CO 3 were used as 
catalysts starting from ( Z)-3ba , however, 41% recovery of ( Z)-
3ba was observed  (Scheme 3, eq 4). These experiments 
indicated that there exist other pathways.  
 
Scheme 3 Mechanistic studies. 
An isotopic labeling experiments using deuterated 
benzaldehyde 
1b -D was conducted. As a result, deuterated 
product 5ba -D was obtained, with 19% D-incorporation in the 
2-position, 34% D-incorporation in the 3-position m ethyl group, 
12% D-incorporation in the 4-position hydroxyl grou p, and 16% 
D-incorporation in the 5-position (eq 5). 
 
Based on the observation above, a possible mechanis m was 
then proposed. N-heterocyclic carbene generated in situ 
reacted with aldehyde to give the Breslow intermedi ate Int-A, 
which would attack the central carbon of the alleno ne 2, 
forming a delocalized anion intermediate Int-B.18  After the 
formation of intermediate Int-B, four pathways are possible: 
(1) An intramolecular D-transfer occurred in interm ediate Int-B 
led to intermediate Int-C and  Int-C’ . Then elimination of the 
NHC produced the deuterated 1,4-enediketones Int-D. With 
NHC acting as a Brønsted base, 18,19  the sequential Aldol 
reaction proceeded to give the final product with d euteration 
within the 2-position and the methyl group of 3-pos ition 
(Scheme 4, route a); (2) H b in Int-B may also transfer to the 
delocalized anion, giving enolate-type intermediate  Int-F. 
Cyclic nucleophilic substitution occurred 20  to give the cyclic 
product 5 with the deuteration in the hydroxyl group, finall y 
yielding the non-deuterated 5, accompanied with the 
regeneration of NHC (Scheme 4, route b); (3) The de uterium in 
the hydroxyl group of Int-F may also transfer to trap the 
enolate, forming α-deuterated intermediate Int-G. Then a 
similar Aldol reaction like route a happened to giv e product 5 
with deuteration at the 5-position via Int-D’ (Scheme 4, route 
a’); (4) Int-G could also form intermediate Int-H followed by a 
pathway like route b to generate product 5 with deuteration at 
the 5-position (Scheme 4, route b’). Meanwhile, the  trans -
diastereoselectivity of products 5 may be explained by the 
stereo-electronic effect of oxygen atom in hydroxyl  group 
adjacent to the NHC acting as a leaving group.

Scheme 4 Possible reaction pathways. 
In conclusion, we have developed an efficient 
diastereoselective
 synthetic route to useful cyclopent-2-
enone-4-ols from readily available aromatic aldehyd es and 1,2-
allenones 2. Mechanistic studies showed the essential role of 
NHC in this transformation. Further investigation i s being 
carried out in our laboratory.
